paper_title: Shuttle Between the Instructions and the Parameters of Large Language   Models
caption: : The induction performance of SHIP and SFT on SNI with respect to the number of observed samples. The accuracy is the average accuracy over all seen and unseen tasks.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of observed samples and the accuracy of two models, SHIP and vanilla SFT. The x-axis is labeled “observed samples” and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 6, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.38 to 0.82, with tick labels at 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8. The line representing SHIP is green, marked with circular data points, and is solid. It begins at approximately 0.81 when x equals 1, fluctuates between 0.79 and 0.81 until x equals 5, and ends at 0.82 when x equals 6. The line representing vanilla SFT is blue, also marked with circular data points, and is solid. It begins at approximately 0.33 when x equals 1, increases to 0.38 when x equals 2, remains at 0.38 when x equals 3, increases to 0.42 when x equals 4, remains at 0.42 when x equals 5, and rises to 0.48 when x equals 6.
